newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Spot baht flat, eyes new minister.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Spot baht flat, eyes new minister.

text.p: Spot Thai baht was flat on Monday as dealers kept books square following the appointment of a new finance minister on Friday.
Dealers said they still did not know if policies would change under Thanong Bidaya or if there would be any more pressure for devaluation.
Thanong was appointed on Friday after Amnuay Viravan quit abruptly following differences with his political rivals in the coalition government of Thai premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
"It is pretty obvious that BOT (Bank of Thailand) wants to squeeze out the specs from the market...and it seems to be working," said a dealer with one U.S. bank in Singapore.
The baht was quoted at 26.000/26.100 to the dollar onshore early on, nearly unchanged from late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.85 per dollar against 25.79.

Thanong pledged at a news conference on Friday he would pursue Amnuay's fiscal and monetary policies, saying they were mostly on the right track in tackling Thailand's worst economic slump in over a decade.
But despite the Thai government's vow it would not devalue the baht, offshore players still believe it may be likely in the future or some changes might be made to the baht system.
In the offshore market, the baht rose to 24.500/24.700 to the dollar from 25.000/25.300 late on Friday on higher buying interest in the baht to cover short position, dealers said.
"We see more buyers (of the baht) now. But it's very quiet, not much activity," said one Singapore-based dealer.
"The buying of dollars in the foreign exchange market remained strong. This may push the interbank rate up slightly today," said one money market dealer.

The dealer said banks also borrowed funds to build up their cash reserves to meet the central bank's next reserve requirement. All commercial banks have to meet the reserve requirement on seventh and 22nd of every month.
The Indonesian rupiah was easier against the dollar in slow trading on the back of adequate rupiah liquidity.

"The rupiah eased slightly amid adequate liquidity, but it is likely to strengthen later as rupiah demand would be up on the month-end factor and half-year book closing," one dealer with a European bank said.
The rupiah was quoted at 2429.50/31.50 at 0430 GMT against an opening of 2429.00/30.00.
"Demand for the local currency should be stronger if the recent rally on the local stock market continues," another bank dealer said.
Dealers said the market remained cautious following political and economic uncertainties in Thailand.
Dealers said offshore investors remained concerned that the Thai problems could spill over to Indonesia, sustaining their overborrowing strategy.
Others said the rupiah was likely to remain strong this month ahead of the end of the financial reporting season.
"They need a lot of rupiah for window dressing," said one Singapore-based analyst. "That should mean dollar/rupiah is effectively capped at 2433."
The Malaysian ringgit fell against the dollar in early Asian trading, pressured by dollar buying by offshore players and strength in the dollar/majors, dealers said.
But corporate selling interest out of Kuala Lumpur would again cap the dollar's rise at 2.5180/90, they said.
By 0430 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5164/69 a dollar against its opening around 2.5155/60 and 2.5150/60 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
For the near term, dealers were expecting the dollar/ringgit to continue trading in the 2.5050-2.5200 range.
Further south, the Singapore dollar stood at 1.4288/99 at 0430 GMT, up from the morning's low of 1.4308.
Dealers said the recovery was based on some cross-trading against the ringgit, which was last quoted at 0.5676 Sing, up from a mid-morning peak at 0.5680.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Chris Johnson in Singapore (65-8703199)
